subject: Microsoft training sales to talk down competitors
posts: Microsoft pivots from partner to predator, training staff to trash-talk the very AI models they once championed. Evidence: Efficiency, Market dominance, Anti-competitive tactics. #Microsoft #AI

Microsoft claims its in-house AI models are more efficient and cost-effective than those from OpenAI or Anthropic, framing the shift as a superior end-to-end system. Stated Judgement: (1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference
Reality reveals a strategic move to lock in customers and protect stock value by undermining former partners now that exclusivity clauses have expired. Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -0.8) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. Microsoft is leveraging its market position to suppress competition after benefiting from their innovation. Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (R_net: 6.2, Uncertainty z: 2)
Microsoft is shifting its sales strategy to aggressively pitch its own AI models over those of OpenAI and Anthropic, despite long-standing financial and technical ties to those same companies.

The Bright Side:
Increased competition in the AI space could eventually drive down costs for enterprise users as companies fight for market share.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in the WHO plane; Microsoft claims to be selling a 'system' (WHAT), but the beneficiary is solely their own bottom line, not the user's actual needs.

Social Physics Analysis:
Microsoft is using a pretext of 'efficiency' to mask a power-hoarding move. By projecting inferiority onto partners, they attempt to maintain dominance without genuine innovation.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The shift prioritizes market control over collaborative progress.

The Unavoidable Truth: Microsoft is a profit-driven corporation protecting its stock price.

The Unavoidable Lie: This strategy is purely about providing a better, more secure end-to-end system for the customer.

Alethekanon:
This is a classic pivot from partnership to enclosure. By commodifying the 'system' to exclude rivals, they reveal the fragility of their original open-model claims.

Awwthekanon:
It is sad to see such a promising collaborative ecosystem turn into a battlefield. Trust is the foundation of innovation, and this move erodes that foundation.

Brothekanon:
Classic corporate move. They build you up, take your tech, and then try to bury you once they've got their own version running. Business as usual, I guess.
